en.runTitle: Brazilian developer and nurse couple from Recife: Express Entry scores, French and a first-three-months budget in Canada

fields.label: My partner and me

fields.value: Me: bachelor’s in computer science, 6 years of full-time backend development in Brazil. Her: bachelor’s in nursing, 4 years of experience

fields.label: CLB or NCLC for each skill
fields.value: IELTS not taken yet; I estimate CLB 8–9 and she estimates CLB 7

en.template: Help me plan Express Entry for {couple}. We are {ages}, with {work}, and we have {savings}. Rebuild the CRS and Federal Skilled Worker scores for each of us as principal applicant using my English and French test levels of {levels}, compare them with the latest rounds, and check the French and healthcare category rules. Rebuild the settlement funds, pre-arrival costs and first three months in {city} with my own prices, and mark anything unconfirmed, placeholder or from memory. Ask before contacting anyone or paying anything.

phases.title: Read the official Express Entry pages, fees and cost sources, build the guide, then run an independent check
phases.judgment: The independent reviewer found four real mistakes in the first draft, among them a French-draw count that should be 3, not 5, and a “46% depreciation” that is really about a 32% loss in the real’s value. All four were fixed, and the guide says plainly that the re-check afterwards was done by the lead colleague, not by the reviewer.

workers: Looked up published prices for language tests, credential assessment and police certificates for applicants in Recife
Built a sourced three-month cost-of-living baseline for a couple arriving in a Canadian city: rent, transit, health cover and the exchange rate
Recomputed every score and money figure on its own and checked the guide against the live government pages
